correctness.rationale: The two-stage walk factors exactly as Q=AB with A(g,x)=1_(gx=x)/f(g), B(x,h)=1_(hx=x)/|H|. The companion point process K=BA is invariant under point stabilizer H; double transitivity forces common off-diagonal (1−a)/(n−1), hence K=Π+λ(I−Π). Burnside’s lemma for the H-action on X gives E_H f=2, and Jensen yields a≥1/2>1/n; identity fixes all n points, so a<1 and 0<λ<1. The formula Q^t=A K^(t−1)B gives π=f/|G| and exact affine interpolation for every t≥1. A one-step row Q(g,.) is a convex mixture of μ_x=Uniform(G_x), with TV(μ_x,π)=1−2/n from exact support comparison; a singleton fixer makes it exact. For S_n the inverse fixed-point count expectation yields truncated exponential; for affine group the stabilizer is identity plus q−2 single-fix nontrivial dilations. Independent Fraction arithmetic checked 497 exact Q²(g,h) comparisons in S_3, S_4 and AGL(1,5), and sharp maxima, corroborating the all-group proof.

final_claim: For finite doubly transitive G acting on n≥3 points, dual Burnside kernel Q on G* has Q^t(g,h)=π(h)+λ^(t−1)(Q(g,h)−π(h)) for every t≥1, π(h)=f(h)/|G|, λ=(na−1)/(n−1)∈(0,1), a=|H|⁻¹Σ_(h∈H)1/f(h). If a singleton-fixing element exists the sharp worst-start TV is (1−2/n)λ^(t−1); λ(S_n)→1−e⁻¹ whereas λ(AGL(1,q))=(q−2)/(q−1). One-step conjugacy-class stationarity is inherited from prior work and is not an originality assertion.
limitations: Requires finite doubly transitive action and t≥1.
Sharp worst-start factor (1−2/n) assumes an element with precisely one fixed point.
No cutoff result or general action-class sampling superiority is established.
